title: STI PCR test
what: The doctor takes a swab, or you give a morning urine sample. The lab looks for germs that cause sexually transmitted infections.
why: For discharge, itching, pain when peeing, after unprotected sex with a new partner, or when planning a pregnancy.
duration: the sample takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: What symptoms you have and since when
If you took antibiotics in the last month
If you used vaginal suppositories or creams
The date of your last period, if you are a woman

prepare.title: Peeing
prepare.text: Do not pee for 2 to 3 hours before the swab. This gives a better sample.

prepare.title: 1 to 2 days before
prepare.text: No sex. Women: no douching, suppositories, or creams. Men: no local antiseptics.

prepare.title: Periods
prepare.text: Swabs are usually not taken during your period.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: If you take antibiotics, tell your doctor. They will decide the best time for the test.

steps: Women sit in the exam chair, and the doctor takes a swab using a speculum
Men usually have a swab taken from the urethra with a thin probe, or give the first part of their urine
The sample goes into a tube and is labeled
feel: Men may feel stinging the first time they pee after the swab. It passes quickly
after: Results usually come in 1 to 3 days. The lab will tell you when
If an infection is found, your partner is usually treated too. Your doctor will decide
Until you get results, avoid sex or use a condom
red_flags: Pain low in the belly with a fever: see a doctor the same day

faq.q: Should I get tested if I have no symptoms?
faq.a: Many infections have no symptoms. If you had unprotected sex with a new partner or are planning a pregnancy, it is better to get tested.
Many clinics offer anonymous testing. Ask your clinic.

reminders.text: STI swab tomorrow. Today, no sex, suppositories, or douching. Do not pee for 2 to 3 hours before the swab.
